messages:
emily: quick note — after landing the token-bucket admission + concat-kernel swap (int8_concat) I'm seeing 95th tail regressions specifically when prefix-cache hit rate > ~60%. attaching short repro and a couple of flame snippets.
raj: hmm, interesting. is this only on long-context requests or any sequence length? :thinking_face:
mike: saw something similar on my perf run yesterday — the batcher stops merging cache-hit prefixes into mixed batches and kernel selection prefers concat path which messes with per-token cost. short dump below.
perf-bot: profile dump uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/2177890123/trace.json
sarah: can you paste the flame? also which queue policy was active? token-bucket vs fair-queue?
emily: flame attached inline — main delta is extra scheduling gap between packer->kernel when a mixed batch (cache-hit + cache-miss) is present. queue policy: token_bucket with budget_target=128, admission_penalty=0.2. batch formation log:
```
[2026-03-12T09:21:03Z] batch_id=962 size=5 tokens_total=420 hit_slots=2 miss_slots=3 kernel=int8_concat selected
[2026-03-12T09:21:03Z] packer_delay_ms=18 admission_delay_ms=34 kernel_start_ms=12
[2026-03-12T09:21:03Z] kvcache_lookup_ms=3 merge_ms=6
```
mike: that admission_delay looks high. token_bucket yields big jitter if hit_slots lower the virtual length but kernel expects contiguous KV runs, so it defers. maybe we need cache-hit-aware virtual_length calc (i.e., weight hits less when computing admission budget).
raj: agreed. current virt_len = sum(token_count / kernel_efficiency_for_type). But kernel_efficiency doesn't account for cache-hit path being way cheaper (KV fast path). proposal: compute virt_len = sum(tokens * (1 - hit_weight) + tokens * hit_weight * hit_cost_factor). basically reduce cost of hits when making admission decisions.
sarah: any regression on throughput when hits are treated lighter? we could starve misses.
emily: tested locally with hit_weight=0.2 and hit_cost_factor=0.15 — admission improved latency tail 95->82 ms on the scenario, throughput stable. but noticed kernel selection flips to int8_fastpath more often which increases CPU->GPU kernel switch overhead for mixed batches.
mike: maybe add a policy: if batch contains both hit/miss and mixed_kernel_change_proba > 0.3 then force homogeneous packing (i.e., split by cache-hit affinity) rather than trying to merge. simple rule: if hit_fraction < 0.4 and miss_slots>1 -> split.
raj: that could increase small-batch overhead. alternative: allow merging but prefer kernel compatible variant: fallback kernel selection to slower but homogeneous-friendly kernel when mixing causes extra prep cost. we need break-even calc.
perf-bot: quick calc: prep_overhead_mixed=12ms, extra_per_token_mixed=0.4us, split_penalty=20ms extra batches. breakeven at batch_size>50 tokens.
emily: thanks — next steps:
- run A/B with hit_weight tuning (0.1/0.2/0.3) on canary (2% traffic) over 24h
- add a metric for "mixed_kernel_switch_ratio" and "split_due_to_cache_affinity"
- add a fallback kernel config flag `prefer_homogeneous_packing_on_mix` default false
mike: i'll wire up the metrics and the canary. raj/sarah can you review the virt_len math patch? PR incoming.
raj: putting lgtm except we should add a smoke test that forces mixed batches with 70% hits to assert no tail > 100ms.
sarah: +1. also document the reason in runtime/notes — this isn't just a packing bug, it's kernel-selection + admission interplay.
emily: awesome — I'll drop the perf graphs and the small replay harness in the PR description. :rocket:
